articles.headline: Bangladesh garment workers win 36pc wage rise
articles.summary: AI summary: After weeks of at times violent protests, Bangladesh's wage board approved a 36 per cent rise in the garment sector's minimum wage to 17,000 taka from January, short of the 30,000 taka workers sought; the industry body puts protest losses at about $428m.

political.reason: Concerns Bangladesh's labour politics, not Pakistan's governance.

social.reason: No direct effect on daily life in Pakistan.

market.reason: Relevant to Pakistani textile exporters competing with Bangladesh for the same buyers.

lean.reason: Includes worker, wage-board and industry voices with attribution.

confidence.reason: Full wire report read with specific, attributed figures.

articles.headline: $150m Punjab education project downgraded
articles.summary: AI summary: The World Bank cut its implementation rating for the $150m Punjab GRADES education project to moderately satisfactory, citing unmobilised technical assistance, missing baseline data and stalled classroom construction, while noting enrolment and early childhood targets were met early.

political.reason: Administrative performance issue, not a governance crisis.

market.reason: Limited relevance to markets beyond donor-financing watchers.

lean.reason: Factual report noting both shortfalls and progress, though no provincial response is included.

confidence.reason: Full article read; based on a single World Bank disclosure without government comment.

economic.reason: Prestige milestone with no immediate effect on jobs or prices.

political.reason: Strengthens Pakistan-China ties and offers a broadly unifying national moment.
